title: Tenali Raman Tale 127

full_text:
A cunning textile merchant named Haridas arrived at the court of Vijayanagara, claiming he possessed a shawl woven of 'Spiritual Lotus Mist'.
He brought an empty, ornate velvet-lined wooden box, opened it before King Krishnadevaraya, and pantomimed unfolding a delicate garment:
'Jahanpanah! Behold this celestial shawl! It is woven from the spiritual mists of Mount Kailash!
It has no physical weight, but its magical threads keep the wearer cool in summer and warm in winter!
However, only a monarch of pure divine intellect can see its subtle celestial blue threads; to fools and incompetents, it appears like empty air!'

The King and the courtiers stared at the empty box.
Terrified of being considered foolish, King Krishnadevaraya nodded vigorously:
'Ah! Yes, indeed! What exquisite azure embroidery! What celestial lightness!'
The courtiers chimed in with competitive flattery:
'Remarkable! The flowers look alive! What peerless weaving!'

The merchant bowed: 'The price for this celestial shawl is only one thousand gold coins!'
The King was on the verge of paying when Tenali Raman stepped forward with an expression of ecstatic admiration:
'Maharaj! The merchant’s shawl is sublime!
Allow me the honor of draping this celestial shawl around Your Majesty’s shoulders right now!'

Tenali reached into the empty box with careful, delicate fingers, pretended to lift the invisible shawl, and draped the empty air across the King's shoulders!
Tenali smoothed the invisible folds over the King’s chest:
'Look at Your Majesty! What divine majesty!
Now, Maharaj, to complete this spiritual transaction, let us pay the merchant in the exact same celestial currency!'

Tenali pulled out his leather purse, held his empty hand over the merchant’s palm, and mimed dropping heavy gold coins into the merchant's hand:
*‘Clink! Clink! Clink!’*
Tenali said:
'Here, Master Haridas! Take these one thousand Celestial Spiritual Gold Coins forged from the golden clouds of heaven!
Like your shawl, these coins have no physical weight, and can only be seen and spent by merchants of pure divine intellect!
Feel their heavy celestial radiance in your purse!'

The merchant stared at his empty hand in frozen horror:
'Tenali! My hand is completely empty! You have paid me with nothing!'

Tenali replied with razor-sharp irony:
'Why, Master Haridas? If an invisible shawl of empty air can be sold to a King for real gold, surely invisible celestial gold coins are the only proper payment for such an ethereal garment!
When you bring a real shawl woven of real silk by real human hands, the King will pay you in real gold!'

The King and the entire court burst into thunderous, body-shaking laughter!
The swindler snatched his empty box and fled from Vijayanagara, while King Krishnadevaraya praised Tenali’s presence of mind, which protected the treasury from vanity.
moral: Pretentious vanity that boasts of appreciating non-existent subtleties is cured by holding an empty mirror.
